notes.407r.a.55: Square brackets are the edition's restorations. In 414v.b.9-10 the restored verb 'gelâze', 'leave, release', is turned into the passive '[be released by]' for English order. 'rite' is fever. Heinrich and Hildegund are sample names.

nodes.text: food that any Christian person may eat, that you shall not
[Now] [I] will, with the help of our Lord [the] holy Christ
and St [Mary] and St Elisabeth and St Anne
and St [John] and the good St Peter and all
God's saints, cure Heinrich [or] Hildegund of the fever
and of all its [evil] ways, in Christ's name,
amen, amen. Gently and well did [St] [Elisabeth] bear St
[John]; gently and well did St [Anne] bear [St] Mary;
gently and well did St [Mary] bear [our] Lord, [the]
holy [Christ]. Just so gently and so well may [the] person
N. [be released by] [the] [fever] and all its evil ways, in Christ's name, amen, amen. After this you shall say three
Our Fathers with three prostrations, and three Hail Marys with three prostrations.
